newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian leading shares edge up after correction.
newsitem.headline: Russian leading shares edge up after correction.

text.p: Leading Russian shares stabilised after falling more than five percent in the first hour of trade. Operators were uncertain whether prices would firm through the day on Monday but said volumes were healthy.
National power utility UES had recovered to $0.4250 at 0900 GMT from a morning low of $0.4100 after $0.4340 at Friday's close on the Russian Trading System.
Rostelekom which led the market down, partly on first quarter earnings published on Friday, had risen to $4.30 from $4.15 and Friday's $4.66.

Market volume was about $30 million in the first hour and a half. "That shows this is not a bear market," said Rye Man and Gor salesman Kirill Maltsev, who like many traders said a correction was in order after the last month's sharp rise.
Traders said there was no panic but declined to gauge the extent of the widely-anticipated downward correction, despite the levelling off of the morning's slide.
"It has turned has a little bit, but it is not racing back up," said a Troika Dialog sales representative.
Second tier trade was quiet as the market concentrated on the dozen leading liquid shares.

Russian operators were seen as the major sellers in the morning and some foreigners stepped in to buy shares. Funds have been flooding the market, sending the RTS index up about 30 percent in the last month, and some investors are still waiting to place money on the market, traders say.
